claims.title: From a small error of Hecke eigenforms to all integral polynomials
claims.hypotheses: Use the integral frame for the weighted denominator condition and the relative density theorem at fixed level away from the auxiliary place. The selected operators act by scalars on the relevant joint systems.
claims.statement: One finite list of systems and coefficients for each tolerance approximates evaluation of all integer polynomials in their eigenvalues, including simultaneously in all the chosen coordinates.
definitions: A Hecke system lists the simultaneous eigenvalues in the selected operator coordinates.

claims.title: Filtering and composing simultaneous polynomial approximations
claims.hypotheses: Work over a nonarchimedean field. Each intermediate evaluation has polynomial approximants, and the chosen test Q is nonzero at every intermediate evaluation used.
claims.statement: Reweight the inner approximants by Q(x)/Q(η) to remove failed tests. Finite composition followed by summing over fibres preserves uniform polynomial approximation.
definitions: An approximation is uniform over all polynomials with integer coefficients.

claims.hypotheses: The fixed-level density theorem at prescribed generic places, integral test operators and their frame bounds, local type construction, and existence of lacunary weight variation at the second auxiliary place hold.
claims.statement: The same finite weighted systems carry the prescribed local tests, lacunary weight and auxiliary type while approximating all integral polynomials on the retained Hecke and scaled Satake-power coordinates.

claims.title: One finite field for the original rational Hecke coordinates
claims.hypotheses: The definite unitary group and a nonzero automorphic eigenform at finite level are fixed. The Hecke operators are rational. The coefficient fields use the chosen isomorphism with the algebraic closure of the local field.
claims.statement: The degree over ℚℓ of the field generated by any finite selection of original coordinates is at most the dimension of the conjugate-form space. One maximal finite selection generates a field containing the entire system.
definitions: A joint conjugate is the entire list transformed by one field automorphism.

claims.title: Which evaluations keep a Hecke error small?
claims.hypotheses: A definite unitary group has positive rank. The algebraic weight is given in its polynomial model, and each finite Hecke translation satisfies the weighted denominator condition.
claims.statement: Transporting the integral coefficient ball gives separating evaluations. Every form is bounded on them and each selected operator preserves their common bound.

claims.title: Where do the forms satisfying the local tests come from?
claims.hypotheses: Weight and level away from a split auxiliary place over ℓ are fixed. The test set is finite. Each tested place is split and hyperspecial, with a different underlying prime from the auxiliary place. Use the automorphic decomposition at finite level.
claims.statement: After refining at the auxiliary place, admissible forms approximate a fixed form with uniform pointwise relative error. Iteration and a finite decomposition give the list used in simultaneous Hecke tests.
